chunks: No other women are lawful for you after this, nor to change your present wives for other women even though their beauty should appeal to you, except those you have married (or those your right hand possesses), and God is watchful of everything.

key_terms.مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ: those whom your right hand possesses (concubines)

ai.seo_question: What are the unique marital restrictions for Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab?
ai.summary: This verse establishes the 'Khatm al-Nisā' (Seal of Wives) for the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), signifying the finality of his marital status and distinguishing his unique legislative authority from that of other Muslims. The exception for 'those whom his right hand possesses' reflects the specific legal context of the early Islamic community, while the emphasis on God's watchfulness underscores the divine precision in preserving the Prophet's household. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of 'Ismah (infallibility) and the purity of the Ahl al-Bayt, as these wives were not merely spouses but key figures in transmitting religious knowledge.
